OL Agent - Stand Alone Evaluations

Standalone deep-dive analyses of individual SEVAL HeroEval runs

Owner: Yohnathan Carletti

Mainline vs CodeGen+Omni — head-to-head (run 597131)Head-to-head 2026-07-01
79.3% Mainline pass 56.7% CG+Omni pass 265 comparable 61 queries Mainline wins 39CG+Omni wins 35Both fail 20
Mainline is the stronger arm on run 597131: 79.3% assertion pass (288/363) vs CodeGen+Omni 56.7% (206/363). The gap is driven almost entirely by 16 of 61 queries where CodeGen+Omni returned no response (98 assertions auto-failed). On the 265 comparable assertions where both arms replied they are near parity — Mainline 79.2% vs CodeGen+Omni 77.7% — trading 39 Mainline wins for 35 CodeGen+Omni wins (171 both-pass, 20 both-fail). The decisive difference is response coverage, not per-assertion quality.
CodeGen failure triage — EmailTriage Primitives (run 576292)Failure triage 2026-06-24
32% CodeGen pass 632 CodeGen fails 470 regressions 203 queries Model 587Missing data 27Assertion 18
632 of 932 CodeGen assertions failed (32% pass) across 203 queries; 470 are regressions where Mainline passed the same check. Top trends: tool-not-invoked (202), CreateRule target-folder-missing (91), missing disambiguation list (55), missing citation (49), write-did-not-persist (49), mock tool response (49), capability refusal (49). Interactive report filters by trend/tool and exports an ADO selection JSON.
CodeGen vs CodeGen+OMNI — head-to-headHead-to-head 2026-06-24
71.8% CodeGen pass 73.8% OMNI pass 347 comparable 61 queries OMNI wins 47CodeGen wins 40Both fail 51
CodeGen+OMNI nets +2.0pp (73.8% vs 71.8%) over 347 comparable assertions. OMNI wins 47 (saves drafts to the Drafts folder, disambiguates); CodeGen wins 40 — but 32 of those are empty / uncaptured OMNI replies on heavy compound tasks (Calendar OOO, Rules), not quality losses. 51 both-fail (folder-delete unsupported, compound multi-step).
HeroV28 Mainline vs CodeGen — both-arm assertion triageFailure triage 2026-06-24
78 both-arm fails 37 queries 466 comparable Model 54Missing data 18Assertion 6
78 of 466 assertions failed in BOTH control and experiment across 37 queries. Root causes: 69% model/agent behavior (HITL confirmation gaps + capability refusals), 23% missing data (empty mailbox), 8% bad assertions (false negatives).
Outlook agent — HeroPrompt V27 single-run reportSingle-run report 2026-06-22
43.1% Query pass 78.5% Assertion score 65 queries 325 assertions Passed 28Failed 37Critical 75.2%
Single-run evaluation of the Outlook agent (gpt-55-reasoning) over the 65-query HeroPrompt V27 hero set: 28 of 65 queries fully passed (43.1%) and 255 of 325 assertions passed (78.5%). By level: critical 75.2% (191/254), expected 89.8% (53/59), aspirational 91.7% (11/12). Execution dimensions are near-ceiling (tool call / code generated / answer generated 100%, execution success 98.5%); the remaining gap is answer-correctness (43.1%). Run cost $32.36 over 18.3M tokens, ~47s average latency. Report merges a filterable per-query list with judge rationales, generated code, and execution traces.
